name: new_pillar_title
title: Prepare a column title for formatting

origin.description: Build the object that format() renders as the column titles.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector of column titles. NULL is an empty title.
Further arguments must be empty. A value here warns, and the title is still built.

origin.details: NULL has width 0. A vector that is entirely missing or "" is stored as NULL and also has width 0. Any other title is padded on the right to the widest name, and that width is stored. pillar.min_title_chars defaults to 20. When the title is no wider than that option, or the option is infinite, the minimum width equals the title width. Otherwise the minimum is the option plus 2, truncated toward zero. format() then paints the titles with the bold style. pillar.bold defaults to false, so the names of trees have no ANSI codes. Girth is one column shorter than Height, so it gains one trailing space.

translation.description: The same titles. None is a null title. A string is one name and a list is the vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string, None, or a list of strings. None, NULL, "", and a list that is entirely missing or blank become a null title. A missing name inside the list is None.

translation.details: The width is the widest name after left alignment. format() uses that stored width when width is omitted, then style_bold. With pillar.bold false the result is plain text. A single name comes back as a string. A list comes back as a list. A null title formats as an empty list. An unexpected keyword is an error, and the message is the same text check_dots_empty prints. A narrow width shortens with an ellipsis. The cut counts graphemes, and a second title that is also too wide is an error.
translation.value: A pillar_title. format() returns a string, a list of strings, or an empty list.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.num_colors": 8, "cli.unicode": True})

from pillar.parts import new_pillar_title

print(new_pillar_title(["Girth", "Height", "Volume"]).format())
